text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein, in a meeting with members of the capital's municipal council, sees Amman as a "model capital city in the Middle East."
- Crown Prince Hassan tells local council members that a role exists for non-governmental agencies in local development.
- Iraqi President Saddam Hussein meets ministers of trade and industry and reviews Iraqi-Jordanian ties.

- Jordan and Iraq agree at the conclusion of the visit of the energy and trade ministers to Baghdad to a higher trade protocol ceiling by $35 million from $220. Iraq approves a higher annual "oil grant" to Jordan by another $50 million from $250.
- Prime Minister Kabariti meets Iraq's Aziz during a stop over on his way back to Baghdad; premier calls for boosting inter-Arab economic relations away from political differences.

- U.S. papers praise King Hussein's role in Middle East peace and say the monarch played a key role in getting the regional peace parties to conclude the Hebron accord on the redeployment of Israeli troops from the West Bank town.
- Analysts and columnists credit king with saving the region from catastrophe.
- Health ministry team undertakes serious talks with World Bank officials in a project to restructure the country's health sector, officials say.
- Jordanian stocks are inclined to improve and investors say demand is currently focused on drug and industrial firms that could gain from Iraqi exports.
- Market sources predict a rise in local rice prices in line with world market trends.
- Jordan and Iraq conclude oil, trade agreements.
